question_en: An investor places a buy-stop, all-or-nothing order for a security. The type of instruction(s) relating to this order is (are) best described as:
explanation_en:
Execution instructions vs. validity instructions
Market order types Examples
Market: order is immediately filled at the best available price
Execution instructions Limit: order is filled at a threshold price or better
All-or-none (AON): entire order is filled or canceled
Day: expires at the end of the trading day
Stop: contingent on a specified price to trigger action
Validity instructions
Good-till-canceled (GTC): order is good until canceled
Market-on-close (MOC): order filled at the day's closing price
Orders to buy or sell securities can include both execution and validity instructions. Execution instructions address how to fill an order with
respect to:
The price at which to buy or sell.
The size (ie, quantity) of the order.
Validity instructions refer to when an order can be filled, as well as how long an unfilled order should remain open before it expires. A stop order
is a type of validity instruction. A stop order does not become executable until the security has traded at a prespecified trigger price (ie, stop
price). A buy-stop order cannot be filled until the security has traded at a price equal to or higher than the stop price.
"All-or-nothing" refers to the quantity of the security to be bought or sold; therefore, it is a type of execution instruction. The investor in this
question would have indicated the number of shares that would be purchased in the buy-stop order. However, by adding the all-or-nothing
instruction, the intermediary cannot fill any of the order unless the entire order can be filled.
(Choices A and B) A buy-stop, all-or-nothing order contains both execution and validity instructions.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\6. TOUGH QB UWORLD-2000 MCQs\6. Equity Investments\6.01 Market Organization And Structure - Answers.pdf
question_en: A market's order book for a stock is listed below: Near the end of a trading day, an investor submits a day order to buy 1,000 shares, limit AUD 40.30. No new bids or offers are submitted before the market closes. Which of the following is most likely to occur?
option_b: The order expires after the investor buys 600 shares.
option_c: The order expires without the investor buying any shares.
explanation_en:
Execution instructions define how an order is filled. A market order instructs the brokerage firm to immediately execute the trade at the current
market price, and a limit order instructs the brokerage firm to execute the trade only at the limit price or better. Validity instructions state the
time frame and conditions in which an order may be filled. A day order is valid for the same day it is issued and expires at the end of that day if
not filled.
In this scenario, an investor submits a limit order to buy 1,000 shares at AUD 40.30, which expires at the end of the day. The prices at which
market participants are willing to buy (sell) are called bid (offer) prices. Therefore, the buyer will look to the offer side of the market to fill the order.
The investor sets a limit price of AUD 40.30, instructing the broker to buy up to 1,000 shares at this price or less. The 600 shares offered below
the limit price are immediately filled (like a market order). Since the market closes shortly afterward, the remaining order is not filled, and it is
canceled (Choices A and C).
Compare market orders with limit orders

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\6. TOUGH QB UWORLD-2000 MCQs\6. Equity Investments\6.01 Market Organization And Structure - Answers.pdf
question_en: Which of the following is (are) most likely an example(s) of a primary market transaction?
option_c: Both a private placement and a seasoned offering
explanation_en:
Primary market transactions occur when issuers sell securities directly to investors to raise capital. Primary market transactions typically
include initial public offerings (IPOs), seasoned offerings, private placements, and shelf registrations for securities such as stocks or bonds.
After issuance, the outstanding shares are traded in the secondary markets, where funds flow between traders and/or investors.
In a private placement, companies sell securities directly to a small group of qualified investors; there are often cheaper issuance costs as less
public disclosure is required. Seasoned offerings are sales of additional shares of a security that was previously issued. Although the company
has already "gone public," these additional shares are new to the market. Therefore, this is a primary offering. Both a private placement and a
seasoned offering are examples of primary market transactions (Choices A and B).

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\6. TOUGH QB UWORLD-2000 MCQs\6. Equity Investments\6.01 Market Organization And Structure - Answers.pdf
question_en: A client instructs a broker to submit a limit order to buy 10,000 shares of a stock at £15 a share. This is best described as a(n):
explanation_en:
Traders send various order instructions to intermediaries (eg, brokers, dealers, exchanges) to place trades. Execution instructions define how
an order is filled, commonly in the form of a market or limit order. A market order prioritizes the speed of execution, whereas a limit order
prioritizes the price. Here, the client instructs the broker to execute the buy limit order only if the price is £15 or below.
(Choice A) Validity instructions specify when an order is filled.
(Choice B) Clearing instructions state how a trade is settled.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\6. TOUGH QB UWORLD-2000 MCQs\6. Equity Investments\6.01 Market Organization And Structure - Answers.pdf
question_en: Which of the following best describes a quote-driven market?
option_a: Dealers and customers trade at dealer bid or ask prices
option_b: Customer buy and sell orders are matched based on price and time precedence
option_c: Brokers search for willing counterparties on behalf of customers seeking to buy or sell
explanation_en:
Quote-driven markets are also called dealer, price-driven, and over-the-counter (OTC) markets. In quote-driven markets, dealers provide
liquidity (ie, make markets) by standing ready to trade at their quoted prices. Most trades are between customers and dealers. Buyers must pay
the price the dealer is willing to sell for (ie, ask or offer price), and sellers must accept the price the dealer is willing to buy at (ie, bid price). Almost
all currency and bond trading as well as OTC stock trading occurs in quote-driven markets.
(Choice B) In order-driven markets, customer buy and sell orders are matched based on price priority and time precedence. All automated
trading systems and nearly all exchanges use order-driven systems.
(Choice C) Brokered markets are those in which brokers search for willing counterparties on behalf of customers. Assets traded in brokered
markets typically share several or all the following characteristics: expensive, unique, trade infrequently, and/or difficult to hold in inventory (eg,
large blocks of stock, fine art masterpieces, real estate).

question_en: An investor buys 100 shares of stock at $78. To limit potential losses, the investor places a "good-till-canceled, stop $72, limit $70" sell order. Later that day, after the market closes, the company announces disappointing financial results. The next day, the stock opens at $69. At this point, the investor's loss is closest to:
explanation_en:
Market orders determine how an order is completed. Execution instructions define how an order is filled, and validity instructions state the
time frame and conditions under which an order is filled. In this scenario, a combination of execution and validity instructions is used:
The instruction "stop $72" is a stop-loss order, used to contain potential losses. Once the stock falls to the stop price or below it, the
execution instructions are triggered.
The instruction "limit $70" links the stop-loss order with a limit order, executing the trade at a price of $70 or better. Since this is a sell order,
the price must be $70 or higher for the order to fill.
In this scenario, the immediate outcome is that no action is taken. The stop is triggered when the price falls below $72. However, the stock opens
$1 below the $70 limit, preventing the order from being filled. As a result, no trade is executed, and the current unrealized loss stands at $900
[(69 − 78) × 100]. The order remains valid (ie, good till canceled), so if the stock price rises to $70 (ie, lowest acceptable limit price), the trade will
be executed.
(Choice A) A $600 loss incorrectly assumes the trade is executed at the stop price of $72.
(Choice B) An $800 loss incorrectly assumes the trade is executed at the limit price of $70.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\6. TOUGH QB UWORLD-2000 MCQs\6. Equity Investments\6.01 Market Organization And Structure - Answers.pdf
question_en: In an order-driven market system, the following buy limit orders for a stock are listed in the system's limit book: Each order is listed for 200 shares. Based on the commonly used order precedence hierarchy, if the current market price is $15.10 and the exchange receives a market sell order for 500 shares, then the orders most likely to be fully executed are:
explanation_en:
Order-driven system: priority rules for filling limit orders
The most aggressively priced orders (eg, highest-priced
Highest priority:
buys, lowest-priced sells) filled first
Price
Price takes priority over time and visibility
Orders of fully visible size have priority over those of partially
Next priority:
or fully hidden size
Visibility
Visibility takes priority over time
Next priority: Same-price orders filled based on time of receipt
Time received Earliest received = Higher priority
An order-driven system is used by nearly every stock exchange, with rules that match the buyers' and sellers' orders. Three basic rules
determine how limit orders are executed ("filled").
The first rule is based on price. Orders with the most aggressive prices (eg, highest buy price, lowest sell price) receive the highest priority. If
more than one order has the same price, priority is given to orders that are fully visible, meaning that the entire number of shares covered by the
order is known. Orders in which the size is hidden, either fully or partially (ie, iceberg orders, have lower priority than fully visible orders.
For orders with the same price and visibility, priority is based on when each order was received. The earliest-received order has the highest
priority, followed by the second earliest, etc.
In this case, Order 3 has the highest price, so it will be filled first even though it arrived last at the exchange. Orders 1 and 2 have the same price.
Order 1 arrived first, but since it is an iceberg order, it drops behind Order 2 in priority. Order 1 receives only 100 shares; Orders 2 and 3 are filled
entirely (Choices A and C).

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\6. TOUGH QB UWORLD-2000 MCQs\6. Equity Investments\6.01 Market Organization And Structure - Answers.pdf
question_en: If dealers provide liquidity in a market, the market is most likely a(n):
explanation_en:
Quote-driven markets are over-the-counter (OTC) markets in which most trades occur between customers and dealers. In quote-driven markets,
dealers provide liquidity (ie, make markets) by standing ready to trade at their quoted prices. Investors can buy or sell only at the price the
dealer is willing to transact. Almost all currency and bond trading, as well as most spot commodity trading, occurs in quote-driven markets (ie,
OTC).
(Choice A) Brokered markets are those in which brokers search for willing counterparties on behalf of customers. Assets traded in brokered
markets typically are expensive, unique, traded infrequently, and/or difficult to hold in inventory (eg, very large blocks of stock, fine art, real estate).
(Choice B) In order-driven markets, buy and sell orders are matched based on price priority and time precedence. All automated trading systems
and nearly all exchanges use order-driven systems.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\6. TOUGH QB UWORLD-2000 MCQs\6. Equity Investments\6.01 Market Organization And Structure - Answers.pdf
question_en: Which of the following is most likely a characteristic of an order-driven market?
option_b: Exchanges use trading rules to match buyers with sellers.
option_c: Brokers arrange transactions between buyers and sellers.
explanation_en:
Exchanges (and alternative trading systems) implement order-driven systems to match buy orders with sell orders based on price-related
rules. As such, anonymous buyers and sellers provide liquidity to one another.
In a quote-driven (ie, price- or dealer-driven) market, market participants trade with dealers directly; therefore, dealers provide liquidity (Choice
A). In a brokered market, brokers arrange trades between willing buyers and sellers for unique instruments (eg, real estate, rare art) or large
positions (Choice C).

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\6. TOUGH QB UWORLD-2000 MCQs\6. Equity Investments\6.01 Market Organization And Structure - Answers.pdf
question_en: The primary distinction between money markets and capital markets is most likely that:
option_a: money market securities have greater risk.
option_b: capital market securities are all debt instruments.
option_c: money market securities mature within a year or less.
explanation_en:
Financial markets can be classified into money markets or capital markets. Money markets contain debt securities that mature in one year or
less, whereas capital markets contain debt and equity securities that have longer (or indefinite) maturities.
Many money market instruments (eg, T-bills) tend to be more liquid and less risky, so they offer lower returns. Capital market instruments (eg,
stocks) are not as liquid and are riskier (ie, tied to underlying company performance) but may offer higher returns (Choices A and B).

question_en: An investor bought 100 shares of stock for $50 per share on 80% margin and paid a $20 commission. The call money rate on the margin loan is 10% per annum. The stock pays an annual dividend of $1 per share. The investor sells the shares a year later for $60 per share and pays a $20 commission. The investor's rate of return for the year is closest to:
explanation_en:
Buying on margin allows investors to acquire a position that is greater than their own capital (ie, equity) since they can purchase an amount equal
to the margin loan plus equity. Trading on margin magnifies both gains and losses.
To determine the investor's return, divide the net profit by the investor's initial outlay. Net profit in this instance equals the investor's profits
after interest and transaction costs (commissions). The investor's initial outlay equals the initial equity plus the commissions on the purchase.
Therefore, the investor's return is 23.88%.
Note that commissions must be accounted for in both the numerator and in the denominator when calculating net total rate of return:
In the numerator, both purchase and sales commissions must be subtracted to derive net profit
In the denominator, purchase commissions must be included as a real expenditure at Time 0, and therefore as part of the total initial outlay.
(Choice B) 24% results from ignoring transaction costs in the denominator. Doing so understates the investor's initial outlay.
(Choice C) 24.12% results from subtracting, instead of adding, the initial purchase transaction costs from the investor's equity in the
denominator. Doing so understates the investor's initial outlay.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\6. TOUGH QB UWORLD-2000 MCQs\6. Equity Investments\6.01 Market Organization And Structure - Answers.pdf
question_en: A trader has BRL 20,000 and wants to buy on margin to obtain a large stock position. If the local brokerage firm has an initial margin requirement of 0.25, then the maximum total value of stocks that can be purchased is closest to:
explanation_en:
Traders often borrow money from brokerages to finance portions of a large purchase. The total funds available to purchase securities equal the
borrowed amount (margin loan) and the trader's capital (equity). The maximum borrowing amount is determined by the initial margin
requirement, which is the minimum ratio of equity to total funds invested. The smaller the initial margin requirement, the more the trader can
borrow.
Rearrange the equation to calculate the maximum amount of funds that can be invested. Note that questions may alternatively quote a leverage
ratio, which is the inverse of the initial margin requirement (eg, leverage ratio of 4 = 1 ÷ 0.25). Simply multiply the equity amount by the leverage
ratio to derive the total funds (ie, 20,000 × 4 = 80,000).
(Choice A) BRL 26,667 results from dividing 20,000 by the fraction of debt (0.75), not equity (0.25).
(Choice B) BRL 60,000 is the margin loan, not the total funds available to purchase stocks.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\6. TOUGH QB UWORLD-2000 MCQs\6. Equity Investments\6.01 Market Organization And Structure - Answers.pdf
question_en: All else equal, if trading liquidity increases in a secondary market, then the effective cost of issuing capital in the primary market will most likely:
explanation_en:
Companies raise money by issuing securities (eg, stocks, bonds) in primary markets. After issuance, these securities trade on secondary
markets. A highly liquid secondary market enables participants to trade securities quickly, which lowers trading costs and reduces investors'
risk. These factors mean that investors are more willing to pay higher prices in the primary markets if liquidity is high in secondary markets.
This in turn lowers a company's effective cost of issuing capital (issuance cost ÷ proceeds) since the company receives more proceeds from
investors during issuance in the primary markets relative to issuance costs (eg, underwriting and legal fees).

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\6. TOUGH QB UWORLD-2000 MCQs\6. Equity Investments\6.01 Market Organization And Structure - Answers.pdf
question_en: A hedge fund manager conducts extensive fundamental analysis on a company. Based on this analysis, the manager believes an upcoming earnings report will disappoint market expectations. The manager plans to profit from this situation by taking a short position in the company's stock. In this decision, the manager is best described as a(n):
explanation_en:
Market participants engage in the financial system to save, borrow, raise equity capital, manage risk, exchange assets, and trade based on
superior information. The financial system best facilitates these uses when markets are liquid, financial services are provided at a low cost,
information is readily available, and regulation is effective.
There are three fundamental types of participants in financial markets:
Pure investors, who use risky portfolios to save and increase wealth for future use (Choice B)
Hedgers, who primarily focus on mitigating potential financial loss (Choice A)
Information-motivated traders, who seek to profit beyond the expected return of holding risky assets by anticipating and reacting to
market data.
However, most participants use financial markets for multiple purposes. For example, active investment managers are often both pure investors
and information-motivated traders. Many active managers construct portfolios that they believe will achieve greater risk-adjusted returns through a
combination of long-term investing and trading to profit from superior information.
In this scenario, the hedge fund manager is an information-motivated trader. By taking a short position in the stock, the manager is seeking to
profit from an event (the upcoming earnings report) in the belief that the firm's research provides an information edge over other market
participants.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\6. TOUGH QB UWORLD-2000 MCQs\6. Equity Investments\6.01 Market Organization And Structure - Answers.pdf
question_en: A leveraged security position is held with only the minimum required equity. If the minimum equity requirement is reduced, the most likely consequence is that the position's risk is:
option_a: increased since the securities are less valuable collateral for the margin loan.
option_b: decreased since the maximum possible loss is reduced by having less equity in the position.
option_c: increased since any security price changes will be a larger percentage of the position's
explanation_en:
In a leveraged position, a trader invests less equity than the security's market value (ie, buys on margin) and borrows the balance. For any
position, leveraged or unleveraged, gains or losses are the change in the position's value. For a leveraged position the equity is less than 100% of
the position's value, therefore any percentage change the position's value will produce a greater percentage change in the equity.
Leveraged long positions exhibit a wider dispersion of returns than unleveraged long positions since the percentage gains (losses) are greater
when prices rise (fall). Therefore, leveraged long positions are riskier. The difference in risk is related directly to the leverage ratio: if a position's
equity is reduced in line with a reduction in the minimum margin requirement, risk increases since the leverage has increased.
(Choice A) The collateral value of securities is based on market value and is not affected by the margin requirement.
(Choice B) Losses are not limited to the trader's equity in the position. Holders of leveraged security positions incur losses equal to the full
amount of any loss on the entire position.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\6. TOUGH QB UWORLD-2000 MCQs\6. Equity Investments\6.01 Market Organization And Structure - Answers.pdf
question_en: An investor is able to subscribe for 100 shares of new-issue stock at a fixed price of $25 per share as a result of already owning 1,000 shares. This transaction is best described as a:
explanation_en:
Companies use several methods to issue securities when raising equity capital. A rights offering is a relatively easy way for companies to raise
new capital by tapping into their existing shareholder base.
In a rights offering, existing shareholders are entitled to purchase, at a predetermined price, additional shares proportional to their existing
holdings. In this scenario, the investor has the right to buy 1 share for every 10 shares owned.
For shareholders, a disadvantage of a rights offering is that it is dilutive, forcing shareholders to commit additional capital to maintain their
proportional ownership. However, there also are advantages for shareholders, including the following:
Rights come at no cost.
Rights are a form of short-term warrant that can often be sold to other investors.
The subscription price is almost always below the market price, resulting in an immediate gain.
(Choice B) In a private placement, restricted shares (ie, shares that can be sold only to qualified investors) are sold directly to a limited number of
qualified investors. Participation in a private placement is not dependent on existing ownership.
(Choice C) A preferred stock offering is typically issued through traditional public offering methods and offers preferred stock, not additional
shares of common stock.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\6. TOUGH QB UWORLD-2000 MCQs\6. Equity Investments\6.01 Market Organization And Structure - Answers.pdf
question_en: Which of the following is least likely a reason for a public company to issue securities through a private placement?
explanation_en:
Companies use many methods to issue securities when raising capital. In a private placement, shares are not offered to all potential investors as
in a public offering. Instead, they are sold directly to a limited number of qualified investors. Private placements have several features that make
them attractive to issuers, including reduced regulatory and disclosure requirements resulting in lower issuance costs than public offerings
(Choices A and C).
Privately placed issues are potentially riskier than securities sold through public offerings. This is due in part to reduced disclosure, which makes
the securities more difficult to evaluate. Further, securities may be illiquid as they typically cannot be traded on organized exchanges until a
specified time has elapsed. Due to the increased risk, private placements can be sold only to a limited number of wealthy, knowledgeable (ie,
qualified) investors. Investors are compensated with higher expected returns (ie, lower offering prices) relative to public offerings.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\6. TOUGH QB UWORLD-2000 MCQs\6. Equity Investments\6.01 Market Organization And Structure - Answers.pdf
question_en: A trader bought 1,000 shares of a non-dividend paying stock on margin for £100 per share. The trader sells the shares 3 months later for £110 per share. The leverage ratio at the time of the purchase was 3. Ignoring interest on the borrowed amount and transaction costs, the rate of return earned by the trader during this period is closest to:
explanation_en:
Traders often borrow money to finance portions of a purchase, a technique that is frequently referred to as "buying on margin." The margin
loan is the borrowed amount, and equity is the trader's own funds. The leverage ratio is the amount of total funds invested (margin loan plus
equity) compared with equity. The greater the leverage (due to the greater proportion of borrowing), the riskier the trader's position since leverage
magnifies both gains and losses.
In this case, the leverage ratio is 3, so the trader acquires an initial position that is 3 times the amount of equity. This also means that the trader's
leveraged return is 3 times the unleveraged return. Had the trade been unleveraged, the return would have been 10%, or (110 – 100) ÷ 100.
However, since the trader bought on margin, the unleveraged return (not considering interest and transaction costs) is multiplied by 3, which
results in a leveraged return of 30%.
(Choice A) 10% is the unleveraged return. Since the trader purchased a position 3 times the initial equity (ie, supplied 33.33% of funds with own
equity), 10% return is multiplied by 3.
(Choice B) 14% results from dividing the unleveraged return by the proportion of margin borrowing, not the initial equity.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\6. TOUGH QB UWORLD-2000 MCQs\6. Equity Investments\6.01 Market Organization And Structure - Answers.pdf
question_en: An investor bought 500 shares of stock on margin at the beginning of the year and sold them all at year-end: Assume that dividends and interest are paid at year-end. If the leverage ratio is 4 and the call money rate is 6%, then the investor's total rate of return over this period is closest to:
explanation_en:
Buying on margin allows investors to acquire a position that is greater than their own capital (equity) since they can purchase an amount equal to
the margin loan plus equity.
To determine an investor's return, divide the net profit or loss by the investor's own initial outlay. Net loss (−2,645) equals the investor's
losses after accounting for dividend income, commissions, and interest expense. The investor's own initial outlay (6,260) equals the initial equity
plus the commissions on the purchase. Here, the investor's return is −42.25%.
Note that commissions must be accounted for in both the numerator and in the denominator when calculating net total rate of return:
In the numerator, both purchase and sales commissions must be subtracted to exclude them from net profit
In the denominator, purchase commissions must be included as a real expenditure at Time 0, and therefore as part of the total initial outlay.
Trading on margin amplifies risk by magnifying gains and losses. Here the stock price declined by 10%, from 50 to 45; however, financial leverage
(from borrowing) magnified the loss by more than 4 times to 42.25%.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\6. TOUGH QB UWORLD-2000 MCQs\6. Equity Investments\6.01 Market Organization And Structure - Answers.pdf
question_en: A trader buys shares of a stock on margin: Based on this information, the margin call price is closest to:
explanation_en:
Investors often borrow money from brokerages to finance portions of a stock purchase (ie, buying on margin). As time passes, the trader's equity
amounts to the value of the stock position net of the margin loan. Downward stock price movements decrease the trader's equity percentage
(equity / value of total stock position), which increases risk to the lender for recovering principal.
Brokerage lenders protect their loaned money by imposing a maintenance margin requirement, which specifies the trader's minimum equity
percentage (40%). If the equity percentage drops below 40% (from stock price declines), then the investor must contribute additional equity.
Otherwise, the brokerage will sell the entire stock position and recoup the loan. The margin call price (233.33) is the stock price that triggers a
margin call .
To conceptually grasp the calculation, understand that the investor initially contributed €560 (denoted E) per share in equity (80% of purchase
i
price × €700 a share). If the stock price drops to €233.33, the trader's equity per share amounts to €93.33, or [560 + (233.33 − 700)]. This results
in an equity percentage of 40% (or 93.33 / 233.33), which equals the maintenance margin. Effectively, if the stock price falls below 233.33, the
investor will receive a margin call since the remaining equity percentage will be below the 40% maintenance margin.
(Choice B) €350.00 results from incorrectly setting 60% (or 1 − 0.4) as the maintenance margin.
(Choice C) €420.00 results from reducing the initial stock price of €700 by 40%.
